name: Southern Crabapple

facts.where: East Texas woods and old homesteads

caution: Very sour and hard raw; always cooked. As with all apples, do not eat the seeds in quantity. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Fragrant pink spring blossoms give way to golf-ball apples too tart to bite. Gather them for the pot, not the hand.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Their sky-high pectin makes crabapples the secret weapon of jelly makers; they also cook into a fragrant apple butter.
